flawed_step: The degree bounds do not imply Hall’s condition: multiple vertices of A may share too few neighbors.
counterexample: Let A={a1,a2}, B={b}, and E={a1b,a2b}. Each vertex of A has degree 1, and b has degree 2. Any matching contains at most one edge, so it cannot saturate both a1 and a2.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The explicit two-to-one star satisfies every hypothesis but has no matching saturating A.
